cards.title: Who supplies required education
cards.front: Connect required education hours to the authorized course provider.
cards.rule: Required appointment and reappointment hours are completed through a course established and offered by the Texas SOS.
cards.boundary: Private study may support preparation while the SOS course supplies statutory fulfillment.
cards.mixup: A private purchase or score does not establish completion in SOSPortal.

cards.title: Separate time limits
cards.front: Keep the course ceiling, assessment timer and fee window distinct.
cards.rule: The course cannot exceed two hours, the guide gives thirty minutes for its assessment, and the course must be taken within ninety days after fee receipt.
cards.boundary: These periods measure different parts of the process. Completion proof also must be within the one year preceding application submission under §§87.13 and 87.14.
cards.mixup: Do not use the ninety-day window as an assessment timer.
cards.source: Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026 — §87.8(c),(d); SOS traditional guide assessment step 7

cards.title: Adopted passing requirement
cards.front: Use the final rule's minimum when reviewing the SOS course.
cards.rule: The adopted initial and continuing education rules require at least seventy percent correct.
cards.boundary: The official item count was not verified from the accessed public sources.
cards.mixup: The proposed eighty-percent figure is superseded by the final adopted seventy-percent minimum.
cards.source: Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026 — §87.8(c);§87.9(c)

cards.title: Course payments and attempts
cards.front: Plan each education attempt as a separate official transaction.
cards.rule: Each initial or continuing course attempt has a separate twenty-dollar nonrefundable fee and a maximum of three completions in three months.
cards.boundary: A fee outside its ninety-day course window is forfeited under the rules.
cards.mixup: A single payment is not an unlimited retry pass.
cards.source: Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026 — §87.5;§87.8(d),(e);§87.9(d),(e)

cards.title: Traditional and online subjects
cards.front: Match official education to the authority being sought.
cards.rule: Traditional and online appointment or renewal use their applicable SOS course subject matter.
cards.boundary: Follow the SOSPortal profile and application instructions for the actual pathway.
cards.mixup: A traditional course alone does not establish every online qualification.
cards.source: Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026 — §87.8(c)(1),(2);§87.9(c)(1),(2)

cards.title: Eligibility continues
cards.front: Treat age, residence and qualification as conditions of office.
cards.rule: Ordinary Texas appointment requires age eighteen, Texas residency and eligibility concerning felony or moral-turpitude convictions.
cards.boundary: Apply the statutory treatment of dispositions and the SOS review to the actual record. Published §87.12 provides its narrow qualified-escrow-officer residency exception for the four listed adjacent states.
cards.mixup: A Texas workplace does not itself replace Texas residency.

cards.title: Bond and personal oath
cards.front: Complete the bond and oath as separate qualification duties.
cards.rule: The ordinary bond amount is ten thousand dollars, and the officer takes the oath before another authorized person before duties.
cards.boundary: State-employee bond provisions have an express statutory exception.
cards.mixup: A bond invoice does not administer the oath, and the applicant cannot execute their own oath.

cards.title: Commission timeline
cards.front: Use qualification and expiration dates to define authority.
cards.rule: An ordinary commission runs four years after qualification, with statewide Texas jurisdiction.
cards.boundary: The reappointment application window opens ninety days before expiration.
cards.mixup: Buying supplies or filing an application does not extend an expired term.

cards.title: Reporting a move
cards.front: Distinguish an address update from leaving Texas residency.
cards.rule: Notify the SOS of an address change by the tenth day after the change.
cards.boundary: Removing residence from Texas vacates the ordinary office.
cards.mixup: A future printed expiration date does not preserve an office vacated by moving out of state.

cards.title: Records when office ends
cards.front: Arrange lawful custody when resignation, removal or death creates a vacancy.
cards.rule: The residence-county clerk obtains the office's record books and public papers under the vacancy provision.
cards.boundary: Statutory retention and online duties also need consideration for their applicable records.
cards.mixup: Resignation does not authorize immediate destruction of the public papers.

cards.title: Traditional physical interaction
cards.front: Understand what physical appearance requires.
cards.rule: For traditional acts the person physically appears in a manner permitting seeing, hearing, communication and provision of identity evidence.
cards.boundary: Online appearance follows its separate authorized standards.
cards.mixup: A courier, telephone call or shared building address does not establish the required interaction.

cards.title: Documentary identity elements
cards.front: Check currentness, issuer, photograph and signature together.
cards.rule: The ordinary acknowledgment documentary route uses a current federal or state government document with the acknowledging person's photograph and signature.
cards.boundary: Other statutory routes include personal knowledge, a qualifying credible witness and the specified residential-real-estate passport route.
cards.mixup: A private photo card does not qualify solely because it has a picture.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.005(a)

cards.title: Credible witness after 2025
cards.front: Apply the current alternative for establishing a credible witness's identity.
cards.rule: The witness may be personally known or present a current federal or state document with the witness's photograph and signature, and the route uses the witness's oath.
cards.boundary: The current text reflects HB4202 effective June 20, 2025.
cards.mixup: Do not repeat the older claim that every credible witness must be personally known.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.005(a)(1)

cards.title: Foreign passport boundary
cards.front: Read the transaction limitation on the special passport route.
cards.rule: A current foreign passport is expressly listed for a deed or other instrument relating to a residential real estate transaction.
cards.boundary: This provision does not make every foreign identity document acceptable for every act.
cards.mixup: The express passport route should not be expanded to unrelated transactions by assumption.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.005(a)(3)

cards.title: Consequences of absent-person acts
cards.front: Remember that appearance has licensing and criminal consequences.
cards.rule: Knowing notarization without the required personal appearance is addressed by §406.0091, with a real-property enhancement.
cards.boundary: The statute includes a specific affirmative defense concerning apparently valid identification presented by an impersonator.
cards.mixup: An affirmative defense is not permission to skip identity or appearance safeguards.

cards.title: Acknowledgment's central act
cards.front: Link acknowledgment to the executing person's statement.
cards.rule: The person appears and acknowledges execution for the purposes and consideration expressed in the instrument.
cards.boundary: Identify the person using the applicable statutory method and complete the certificate.
cards.mixup: An identity check alone does not perform the acknowledgment.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.004;§121.005

cards.title: Representative acknowledgment
cards.front: Identify the individual who actually appears in a representative capacity.
cards.rule: Chapter 121 addresses attorney-in-fact, partnership, corporate, fiduciary and LLC acknowledgments.
cards.boundary: The certificate should match the appearing person's actual stated capacity and execution.
cards.mixup: Do not describe an absent principal or every business owner as physically present.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.006(b)

cards.title: Certificate execution
cards.front: Complete all certificate actions required for an acknowledgment.
cards.rule: The officer makes, signs and seals the certificate of acknowledgment.
cards.boundary: Appropriate forms may be adapted as circumstances require under Chapter 121.
cards.mixup: A seal alone does not supply the officer's required signature.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.004(b);§121.006(a)

cards.title: Short-form identity wording
cards.front: Separate identity verification from the wording exception.
cards.rule: Section 121.005(b) excepts authorized short forms from its identity-method notation requirement.
cards.boundary: The substantive duty to know or satisfactorily identify the person remains.
cards.mixup: A short certificate does not waive identity or appearance.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.005(a),(b);§121.008

cards.title: Corporate employment and ownership
cards.front: Evaluate employment and officer-shareholder conditions accurately.
cards.rule: Corporate employment alone does not disqualify an employee from the stated acknowledgment or proof.
cards.boundary: The statute separately treats an officer-shareholder owning over one-tenth of one percent in a corporation with one thousand or fewer shareholders.
cards.mixup: A rule about employment alone does not erase all other restrictions.
cards.source: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121 — §121.002

cards.title: Solemn act before certification
cards.front: Ensure the affiant actually makes the oath or affirmation.
cards.rule: An oath-based act requires the actual solemn commitment described by its certificate.
cards.boundary: The SOS supplies definitions and sample jurat and verification materials.
cards.mixup: Silently watching a signature does not administer a solemn promise.
cards.source: Texas SOS public notary educational information — Definitions and sample forms

cards.title: Affirmation choice
cards.front: Recognize affirmation as an available solemn form.
cards.rule: The official materials recognize affirmation alongside the oath, and the qualification statute expressly allows affirmation.
cards.boundary: Use the act and certificate appropriate to the transaction.
cards.mixup: A person's preference for affirmation does not justify omitting the solemn commitment.

cards.title: Physical inability safeguards
cards.front: Use the statutory procedure for signing an individual's name only with its safeguards.
cards.rule: The individual must physically be unable to sign or make a mark, direct the notary, and have a qualifying disinterested witness present.
cards.boundary: Identify the witness using the standard incorporated from §121.005.
cards.mixup: Convenience alone does not satisfy the statutory physical-impairment definition.

cards.title: Assisted-signature annotation
cards.front: Record how the notary-affixed signature was made.
cards.rule: Place the prescribed or substantially similar statement beneath the signature identifying the witness and §406.0165 procedure.
cards.boundary: A compliant signature is effective as the individual's signature under subsection (c).
cards.mixup: The ordinary seal does not replace this separate notation.

cards.title: Online oath record
cards.front: Preserve the remote solemn act even when no document is signed.
cards.rule: An online oath or affirmation requires identification, video/audio recording and retention under §§406.1107 and 406.108.
cards.boundary: Apply other governing law where the online-oath statute states that qualification.
cards.mixup: An oral online act does not eliminate recording duties.

cards.title: Two transaction dates
cards.front: Preserve the instrument date and act date separately.
cards.rule: The ordinary record includes both the date of the instrument and date of notarization.
cards.boundary: Different dates may accurately describe the same transaction.
cards.mixup: Do not copy one date into both fields without checking the facts.

cards.title: Record content beyond identity
cards.front: Capture the statutory instrument, participant and land details.
cards.rule: Section 406.014 lists signer and grantee information, identification or introducer details, description and applicable land or proof-witness information.
cards.boundary: Apply the specific fields to the actual instrument and procedure.
cards.mixup: A daily transaction count cannot replace the required entries.

cards.title: Public book access
cards.front: Handle certified record requests under the public-information provision.
cards.rule: Book entries are public information and certified copies must be supplied to any requester on payment of all fees.
cards.boundary: This status makes compliance with prohibited sensitive-data entries especially important.
cards.mixup: The requester need not be the original signer under §406.014(c).

cards.title: Numbers and biometrics
cards.front: Use lawful record fields without importing prohibited identifiers.
cards.rule: The published rule prohibits governmental ID numbers, other identifying numbers and biometric identifiers in the record book, while preserving mailing-address numbers.
cards.boundary: The rule excepts the required online audio-visual recording, and the statute allows credential expiration dates.
cards.mixup: An expiration date permission does not authorize a full driver's license number.
cards.source: Texas SOS published Chapter 87 rules — §87.50; Government Code §406.014(f)

cards.title: Ten-year ordinary retention
cards.front: Measure the current ordinary record period from each act.
cards.rule: Section 406.014(g) requires retaining its subsection (a) records until the tenth anniversary of notarization.
cards.boundary: Online electronic records have an additional five-year provision under §406.108(c).
cards.mixup: Do not use commission expiration as the deletion date or assume one period cancels the other.

cards.title: Seal identity
cards.front: Make the seal identify the commissioned officer and term.
cards.rule: Required elements include the Texas notary wording around a five-point star, name, SOS identifying number and commission expiration.
cards.boundary: Use the correct information for the actual commission.
cards.mixup: The notary's driver's license number is not the SOS identifying number.

cards.title: Seal dimensions and border
cards.front: Check physical design against the authorized forms.
cards.rule: A circular seal may be at most two inches in diameter, or a rectangle at most one inch wide by two and one-half inches long, with a serrated or milled border.
cards.boundary: Required content still must fit and reproduce legibly.
cards.mixup: A seal that fits the page can still exceed the statutory dimensions.

cards.title: Legible permanent impression
cards.front: Use a seal impression that survives ordinary reproduction.
cards.rule: The stamped impression uses indelible ink and legibly reproduces required elements by photographic methods.
cards.boundary: Electronically transmitted authenticated documents still must reproduce the required elements legibly.
cards.mixup: A premium stamp price does not prove a particular impression is readable.

cards.title: Restricted seal use
cards.front: Authenticate only the actual official act.
cards.rule: The statute bars supplying a seal copy to another person and attaching the seal except to authenticate the notary's official act.
cards.boundary: Apply specific official filing obligations through their authorized process.
cards.mixup: Blank stationery and marketing artwork do not become official acts because a customer requests them.

cards.title: Online certificate details
cards.front: Make the electronic certificate describe the real method and signature form.
cards.rule: The certificate includes required notary authentication and act facts, plus an online notation and tangible-versus-electronic signature indication.
cards.boundary: The required method indication also appears in the acknowledgment form framework.
cards.mixup: A platform logo cannot substitute for prescribed certificate facts.

cards.title: Signature counting
cards.front: Count signatures covered by one acknowledgment certificate.
cards.rule: For signatures covered by one acknowledgment certificate, the stated fee is ten dollars for the first signature plus one dollar for each additional signature.
cards.boundary: The amount includes certificate and seal. The SOS separately illustrates a fee for each separate certificate, so establish the certificate arrangement before quoting.
cards.mixup: Do not apply the one-certificate total to separate certificates or add another seal fee to its included components.
cards.source: Government Code 406.024(a)(5); SOS Online Notary Educational Information, FAQ 9

cards.title: Oath and residual categories
cards.front: Identify the particular authorized service before charging.
cards.rule: The schedule gives ten dollars for an oath or affirmation with certificate and seal, and specified ten-dollar residual categories.
cards.boundary: A residual category does not turn each administrative step into another notarial act.
cards.mixup: Typing and clicking are not automatically separate official acts under the fee schedule.

cards.title: Copy and deposition units
cards.front: Keep page-based and word-based rates distinct.
cards.rule: Copies in the notary's office are one dollar per page, while taking a deposition is one dollar per hundred words.
cards.boundary: Swearing a deposition witness has its own listed ten-dollar category.
cards.mixup: One dollar per word is not the statutory deposition rate.

cards.title: Online supplement
cards.front: Add the authorized online category only when the lawful online service occurs.
cards.rule: An online notary or employer may charge up to twenty-five dollars in addition to authorized §406.024 fees.
cards.boundary: An online application charge is a qualification expense and a different transaction.
cards.mixup: The twenty-five-dollar supplement is not a per-minute video rate.

cards.title: Current schedule and state charges
cards.front: Distinguish state qualification payments from customer-service fees.
cards.rule: The ordinary statutory filing components total twenty-one dollars, while education has its separate course fee and official acts have §406.024 limits.
cards.boundary: The statute provides periodic SOS inflation adjustment of service fees, so verify the current schedule.
cards.mixup: The ten-thousand-dollar bond face amount is neither a course fee nor a customer notarial fee.

cards.title: Copy certification boundary
cards.front: Check recordability before offering notary-certified copies.
cards.rule: Texas grants copy certification for documents not recordable in public records.
cards.boundary: Official public-record copies should be obtained from the authorized custodian.
cards.mixup: A notary stamp does not make a replacement official birth record.

cards.title: Legal advice and representation
cards.front: Keep the notarial commission's authority within its statutory grant.
cards.rule: A notary without Texas legal licensure may not give or accept fees for legal advice, and §406.017 regulates specified representation.
cards.boundary: Compensated translation and typing have a stated exception under §406.017(a-1).
cards.mixup: That exception does not confer a law license or general immigration representation authority.

cards.title: Advertising in other languages
cards.front: Include the required conspicuous notice in the right languages.
cards.rule: The nonattorney notice includes English and the advertisement's language, permitted fees and the prescribed message.
cards.boundary: Radio and television may modify the statement while retaining substantially the same message.
cards.mixup: A bilingual notice does not independently authorize a separately prohibited notario title.

cards.title: Discipline and process
cards.front: Recognize the SOS enforcement authority and procedural protections.
cards.rule: For good cause the SOS may reject an application or suspend or revoke a commission, with notice, hearing, adjudication and appeal rights.
cards.boundary: The statute specifies district court of Travis County and a de novo appeal trial.
cards.mixup: Paying the application fee does not prevent action on false statements or duty violations.

cards.title: Office does not issue IDs
cards.front: Separate identity verification from identity-document issuance.
cards.rule: A Texas notary may verify identity through lawful procedures but may not issue an identification card.
cards.boundary: The notarial role remains limited to authorized acts.
cards.mixup: A seal on an employee badge cannot confer government identification authority.

cards.title: Two identity processes
cards.front: Distinguish the credential's validity from the individual's identity.
cards.rule: Credential analysis evaluates the identification credential and identity proofing evaluates the individual through the statutory third-party process.
cards.boundary: When using the direct-credential branch in section 406.110(b)(2), combine both processes with remote presentation. Rule 87.41(d)(2) separately recognizes a qualifying credible witness who personally knows the principal and is known to the notary or identified under paragraph (3).
cards.mixup: A clear photograph alone does not complete the full statutory alternative.

cards.title: Exclusive electronic control
cards.front: Protect the signature, seal and record against another person's use.
cards.rule: Keep the electronic record, signature and seal secure and under exclusive control and use the official electronic signature only for online notarization.
cards.boundary: The statute separately requires notifications for theft, vandalism, loss or another person's use.
cards.mixup: A trusted assistant cannot borrow the notary's official signing tools.

cards.title: Tamper evidence and current credentials
cards.front: Preserve verifiability of the electronic notarized document.
cards.rule: The signature device must be current and unrevoked, and attachment must allow independent verification and reveal subsequent changes.
cards.boundary: The SOS application instructions require a compliant third-party X.509/PKI certificate and electronic seal.
cards.mixup: A pasted signature image is not proof that the security requirements are met.

cards.title: Tangible document pathway
cards.front: Apply the paper-document safeguards within lawful online authority.
cards.rule: The notary must reasonably confirm the same document, with a statutory procedure recording signing and declaration, sending by day three and receipt by day ten.
cards.boundary: Section 406.1103(e) preserves other procedures satisfying the same-document requirement.
cards.mixup: Do not treat an ordinary video call and later envelope as automatic compliance.

cards.title: Electronic records and backup
cards.front: Preserve the online act's evidence as well as its result.
cards.rule: Online records include date/time, act/document details, principal information, identity evidence, recording and any fee, with backup and protection.
cards.boundary: Section 406.108(c) states at least five years for its electronic record while other applicable record duties continue.
cards.mixup: The customer's receipt alone does not preserve the online notarial record.

education.summary: Use the 2026 SOS education pathway for initial and renewal applications, distinguishing its course, assessment and application steps.

sections.heading: Complete the right official course
sections.body: The adopted rules apply to appointment and reappointment applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026. Initial applicants complete the SOS education requirement before applying, and returning notaries complete continuing education before applying for reappointment. Traditional and online subject matter are addressed separately. Government Code §406.023 reserves the required hours to a course established and offered by the Secretary of State. This site supplies independent Practice Questions and Course Review. Its study activity does not supply the statutory education hours or an official completion credential.

sections.heading: Track the three time measures
sections.body: The course cannot exceed two hours under §§87.8 and 87.9. The SOS portal guides give thirty minutes for the assessment, require the videos to be completed, and warn that failing to select final Submit produces a zero score and forfeits the attempt. The adopted passing minimum is seventy percent. Each taking costs a separate nonrefundable twenty dollars. Take the course by the ninetieth day after SOS receives the fee, with no more than three completions in three months. The public official assessment item count was not verified. Source check November 14, 2026, 1 TAC §§87.5,87.8,87.9 and the official portal guides. Adopted §§87.13 and 87.14 require completion proof within the one year preceding application submission, separate from the ninety-day fee window. Required course-fee payment proof is also part of the adopted application conditions.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A renewal applicant reads an old voluntary-training page, pays for a private review course and prepares to file. Her November 2026 reappointment uses the continuing education rule. She first finds her existing portal profile, pays for and completes the SOS continuing education, and submits its assessment properly. Her private review can help her understand duties, while only the SOS course fulfills required hours. The thirty-minute assessment timer must be considered separately from the ninety-day course-payment window.

keyFacts: Applications from January 1, 2026 use the adopted education rules.
The adopted minimum is seventy percent correct.
Each official course taking has a separate twenty-dollar nonrefundable fee.
The public assessment question count remains unverified.
Course-completion proof must fall within the one year preceding application submission.

appointment.summary: Follow the individual commission from eligibility and bond through qualification, renewal, address changes and eventual custody of records.

sections.heading: Qualify before undertaking duties
sections.body: Government Code §§406.004–406.010 establish the ordinary pathway. The applicant must be at least eighteen, reside in Texas and satisfy the eligibility rules concerning convictions. Submit the prescribed application and officer statement, satisfy education, provide the ordinary ten-thousand-dollar surety bond and pay applicable filing fees. The statutory filing components total twenty-one dollars for an ordinary bonded appointment. Course charges, bond premiums and portal transaction charges are separate. The bond has a specific state-officer or employee exception, and the SOS provides a separate state-employee process. Published §87.12 provides a narrow residency exception for qualified escrow officers in New Mexico, Oklahoma, Arkansas or Louisiana who satisfy its conditions.

sections.heading: Manage the term and changes
sections.body: An ordinary commission expires four years after qualification and has statewide Texas jurisdiction. Take the official oath before another authorized person before performing duties. A reappointment application may be made no earlier than ninety days before expiration and uses current continuing education. A filing does not prolong an expired term. Notify the SOS of address changes by the tenth day, and recognize that removing residence from Texas vacates the office. Resignation, removal and death trigger the residence-county clerk record-transfer provision. Source check November 14, 2026, Government Code §§406.002–406.022.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A notary plans to move permanently to New Mexico halfway through a term and assumes the printed expiration allows two more years of work. Section 406.020 makes leaving Texas residence a vacancy event. The officer should follow the resulting custody and reporting requirements instead of relying on the date printed on the old seal. If later seeking a new Texas appointment, qualification must be established through the applicable current process.

keyFacts: Ordinary appointment requires Texas residency and age eighteen.
The ordinary bond amount is ten thousand dollars.
The oath cannot be executed before oneself.
Address-change notice is due by the tenth day after the change.

appearance.summary: Establish lawful appearance and the actual identity basis before completing a certificate, using the current 2025 identity amendments.

sections.heading: Physical and online appearance
sections.body: Government Code §406.0091 defines traditional appearance as physical presence allowing the officer and person to see, hear, communicate and provide identification to each other. An absent signer cannot be replaced by a courier, a receptionist or an informal telephone confirmation. Online appearance uses interactive two-way audio and video meeting the online standards, with the required online authority and procedures. Knowing absent-person notarization has a statutory criminal provision and can also be good cause for licensing action. Its real-property condition carries an enhanced classification.

sections.heading: Current acknowledgment identity routes
sections.body: Civil Practice and Remedies Code §121.005 permits personal knowledge or listed satisfactory evidence. The ordinary documentary route requires a current federal or state government document bearing photograph and signature. A credible witness gives an oath and may be personally known or establish identity through the current qualifying federal or state document alternative. HB4202 changed that witness provision effective June 20, 2025. A current foreign passport is expressly listed for a deed or other instrument relating to residential real estate. Apply that transaction boundary carefully. Source check November 14, 2026, §§121.005 and 406.0091.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: An unknown homeowner appears for an acknowledgment without a card. A witness who is also unknown to the notary presents current qualifying state identification with photograph and signature and is willing to give the required credible-witness oath. The current statute provides a route for identifying that witness. The notary must evaluate all conditions and obtain the oath, rather than reject solely because an older guide said every witness must already be personally known.

keyFacts: Traditional appearance is contemporaneous physical interaction.
Documentary identity requires the listed issuer and currentness elements.
The current credible-witness provision has an identification alternative.
The foreign-passport provision expressly concerns residential real estate.

acknowledgments.summary: Connect the executing person, representative capacity, identity method and completed certificate to the acknowledgment that actually occurred.

sections.heading: Obtain acknowledgment of execution
sections.body: Section 121.004 requires the executing person to appear and state that the instrument was executed for its expressed purposes and consideration. Identity verification under §121.005 supports that act. A preexisting signature does not excuse the personal acknowledgment, and a successful identification does not by itself supply it. The officer then makes, signs and seals the certificate. The certificate records the statutory procedure and actual facts. It does not give a nonlawyer notary authority to advise whether a transaction provides desirable legal protection.

sections.heading: Representatives and form boundaries
sections.body: Section 121.006 addresses execution by attorneys-in-fact, partnership representatives, corporate officers or agents, fiduciaries and LLC representatives. Identify the actual appearing individual and stated capacity. Forms may be adapted to circumstances, and the authorized short-form exception concerns the identity-method wording requirement while preserving identity verification itself. The acknowledgment form framework also indicates the lawful appearance method. Corporate employment alone is addressed separately from the officer-shareholder conditions in §121.002. Source check November 14, 2026, Civil Practice and Remedies Code §§121.002–121.008.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: An LLC manager brings a signed agreement and appears with adequate identity evidence. The manager acknowledges executing the instrument in the stated capacity as the LLC act. The notary completes the appropriate representative certificate reflecting this manager and the actual appearance. Naming every absent member as present would misdescribe the event. The notary also avoids assuring the manager that the document creates a particular legal result.

keyFacts: The executing person must acknowledge execution.
Identity and acknowledgment are separate procedural requirements.
The officer makes, signs and seals the certificate.
Representative wording follows the appearing person and actual stated capacity.

oaths.summary: Administer the solemn act described in the certificate and use the statutory safeguards for physical inability to sign and for remote oaths.

sections.heading: Perform the solemn commitment
sections.body: Government Code §406.016 authorizes administering oaths and the official SOS material explains affirmations and jurat forms. An affiant must actually make the appropriate oath or affirmation. Watching a signature silently does not perform that step. Match the certificate to the event, including its actual date and participants. The oath concerns the affiant solemnly adopting the statements and does not make the notary an independent investigator of every fact. Qualification oaths also may be affirmed under §406.010(d).

sections.heading: Accessible and online procedures
sections.body: Under §406.0165, a notary may sign an individual name when physical impairment prevents signing or making a mark, the individual directs the act and a disinterested witness is present. Identify the witness under the incorporated §121.005 standard and add the required or substantially similar notation below the signature. Convenience alone does not satisfy the definition. Separately, §406.1107 requires identification, audio-video recording and retention for a lawful online oath or affirmation. Source check November 14, 2026, Government Code §§406.010,406.016,406.0165,406.1107 and SOS definitions.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A person whose impairment prevents signing or making a mark directs the notary to sign their name. A witness who has an interest in the affected property is proposed. Section 406.0165 requires a witness with no legal or equitable interest in that property, so the proposed witness does not meet that safeguard. Arrange a qualifying witness and complete the identification and notation requirements before relying on this procedure.

keyFacts: An oath or affirmation requires the actual solemn act.
The assisted-signature procedure requires the individual direction.
The assisted-signature witness must be disinterested and properly identified.
A lawful online oath still requires its recording and retention.

records.summary: Build records that preserve the statutory transaction details, protect sensitive identifiers and survive the current retention period.

sections.heading: Collect the listed transaction information
sections.body: Government Code §406.014 lists instrument and notarization dates separately, the signer name and mailing address, the actual identity or introduction method, and applicable witness, grantee and land details. A brief instrument description is included. Capture the facts of each instrument rather than keeping only daily totals. A no-fee act remains subject to the ordinary record obligation unless a specific statutory exception applies. The statute permits electronic storage, and book entries are public information. Any requester who pays all required fees may request a certified copy of an official-act entry.

sections.heading: Sensitive data and duration
sections.body: The published §87.50 rule prohibits governmental identification numbers, other identifying numbers and biometrics in the notary record book while preserving mailing-address numbers. It excepts the required online recording. Section 406.014(f) allows recording the presented identification expiration date. Current §406.014(g), added by SB693 effective September 1, 2025, requires keeping its subsection (a) records until the tenth anniversary of notarization. The separate online electronic-record rule states at least five years under §406.108(c). Apply each applicable duty without assuming one cancels another. Source check November 14, 2026.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A notary record application offers fields for a full driver license number, thumbprint, credential expiration and mailing address. The officer configures the ordinary book to omit the prohibited number and biometric fields while retaining required address and identity-method information and any permitted expiration date. When renewing the commission, the officer archives the old entries so their ten-year retention continues. Changing software does not authorize deleting them.

keyFacts: Record instrument date and notarization date distinctly.
Ordinary book entries are public information.
The ordinary record book excludes prohibited identification numbers and biometrics.
Current subsection (a) records are retained until the tenth anniversary of notarization.

seals.summary: Use a compliant seal and complete certificates that accurately identify the officer, term, act and method of appearance.

sections.heading: Physical design and official use
sections.body: Government Code §406.013 requires the Texas notary wording around a five-point star, the notary name, identifying number and expiration. A circular seal may be at most two inches in diameter, or the rectangular form at most one inch wide by two and one-half inches long. The border is serrated or milled. Stamped impressions use indelible ink and must reproduce required elements legibly by photographic methods. The statute also restricts supplying seal copies and attaching a seal except to authenticate the actual official act.

sections.heading: Certificate and electronic authentication
sections.body: For an acknowledgment the officer makes, signs and seals the certificate under §121.004. The notary signs official instruments in the commissioned name under §406.016(b). The current commission expiration belongs on the seal, including after renewal. An electronic certificate has the elements in §406.101(4), and §406.110(d) requires an online notation and indication of tangible or electronic signature. Electronic attachment also must support independent verification and evident subsequent changes under §406.109(d). Source check November 14, 2026, the cited Government Code and Chapter 121 provisions.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A renewed notary receives a stamp that retains the former expiration and leaves out the identifying number. The name alone does not satisfy §406.013. The officer obtains a compliant seal with the current commission details and checks that an actual impression reproduces clearly. An otherwise correct acknowledgment certificate also needs the officer signature, so the stamp cannot substitute for signing the certificate.

keyFacts: The seal includes the SOS identifying number and expiration.
The statute specifies dimensions and a serrated or milled border.
Use the seal to authenticate the actual official act.
Online certificates indicate online method and signature form.

fees.summary: Identify the authorized service and counting unit before calculating the customer fee, keeping qualification charges in their own budget.

sections.heading: Use the statutory fee category
sections.body: For signatures covered by one acknowledgment certificate, section 406.024(a)(5) provides ten dollars for the first signature and one dollar for each additional signature, including certificate and seal. The SOS Online Notary Educational Information FAQ 9 distinguishes separate certificates, which each have their own fee calculation. It supplies ten-dollar categories for oaths or affirmations, certain certificates and other listed acts. Copies in the notary office are one dollar per page, while taking depositions uses one dollar per hundred words and swearing the deposition witness has its separate category. Protest services also have specific amounts. The official-act charge may not exceed the authorized amount.

sections.heading: Supplements, state payments and currentness
sections.body: Section 406.111 permits up to twenty-five dollars for performing an online notarization in addition to authorized §406.024 fees. It is not a per-minute call rate. The ordinary application filing components under §406.007 total twenty-one dollars, and the education course fee under §87.5 is twenty dollars per taking. Those are qualification payments rather than customer act fees. Section 406.024(c) provides for SOS inflation adjustments once every five years, so consult the current official schedule when quoting a real service. Source check November 14, 2026.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A notary acknowledges three signatures on one deed in one acknowledgment certificate using the ordinary schedule. The first signature permits ten dollars and the two additional signatures permit one dollar each, giving a twelve-dollar acknowledgment maximum. A separate ten-dollar seal charge would duplicate an included component. If a lawful online notarization is also performed, consider the separate §406.111 supplement under its own conditions.

keyFacts: The first acknowledged signature has a ten-dollar category.
For one acknowledgment certificate, additional signatures on the instrument are one dollar each.
The online supplement is up to twenty-five dollars.
Course and application payments are separate from customer act fees.

ethics.summary: Apply the public office within its granted authority, including copy limits, legal-advice boundaries, advertising rules and enforcement provisions.

sections.heading: Authority and prohibited representation
sections.body: Section 406.016 permits certification of copies of documents not recordable in public records. A public-record custodian is the appropriate source for its official certified record. A notary cannot issue identification cards. A notary without Texas legal licensure cannot give or accept fees for legal advice. Section 406.017 separately regulates implying attorney status, specified compensated representation and efforts to obtain government relief. Its exception for translation and typing does not confer a general law license or immigration-representation role.

sections.heading: Communicate and maintain duties accurately
sections.body: Nonlawyer notarial advertising using notario or notario publico is specifically restricted. Other-language advertising requires the conspicuous notice in English and the advertisement language, including permitted fees and the prescribed nonattorney message. Broadcast language may be modified while retaining substantially the same message. The SOS may take licensing action for good cause including false application statements, absent-person acts and failure to maintain records, with the procedural protections in §406.009. Source check November 14, 2026, Government Code §§406.009,406.016–406.018.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: A bilingual office offers translation, typing and notarization. A customer asks the notary to select immigration claims and represent the customer for an additional fee. Ordinary translation and typing have an express exception in §406.017(a-1), but that does not supply authority for the requested legal representation. The office also reviews its advertisement for the required bilingual notice and avoids the separately prohibited notario advertising phrase.

keyFacts: Notarial authority does not include issuing identification cards.
Copy certification has a nonrecordable-document boundary.
Other-language advertisements have specific notice requirements.
Record failures are an express listed good-cause ground.

online.summary: Follow the separate online authority and technology pathway while preserving secure appearance, identity, document and record safeguards.

sections.heading: Authority, identity and security
sections.body: The SOS operational Getting Started instructions require a current Texas traditional commission before the online application path and direct traditional renewal before online renewal. Current rules require applicable online SOS education. Obtain the compliant digital certificate and electronic seal, with the published instructions describing X.509 and PKI. The online notary must be physically in Texas under 1 TAC 87.41(b) and use the required two-way audio-video. The direct-credential branch under section 406.110(b)(2) combines remote credential presentation, credential analysis and identity proofing. Rule 87.41(d)(2) also recognizes an oath from a credible witness who personally knows the principal and is personally known to the online notary or identified under paragraph (3). Keep the electronic record, signature and seal under exclusive control and meet validity and tamper-evidence requirements. The published online application fee is fifty dollars plus current portal payment charges.

sections.heading: Records and tangible instruments
sections.body: Section 406.108 lists online date/time, act and document description, principal information, identity evidence, recording and any fee. Maintain a protected backup and at least the provision stated retention, alongside other applicable duties. Tangible online acts require reasonable confirmation of the same document under §406.1103. Its specified acknowledgment procedure records signing and declaration, requires sending by day three and receipt by day ten, followed by the prescribed certificate. Other procedures satisfying subsection (a) remain possible under subsection (e). Source check November 14, 2026, Government Code §§406.108–406.1107.

example.heading: Worked example
example.body: An online notary receives a wet-ink document that differs from the version displayed in the recorded session. A matching page count does not establish the same document under §406.1103(a). The notary must resolve the discrepancy through a lawful procedure before certification. The specified statutory path also has its declaration, recorded signing, sending and receipt deadlines, so ordinary shipping plus a video call is insufficient by itself.

keyFacts: Online authority ends with the traditional commission under SOS guidance.
The nonpersonal-knowledge method combines three identity components.
Electronic credentials remain under exclusive control.
Tangible online acts have same-document safeguards.

articles.title: Texas Notary Education in 2026
articles.description: Plan the SOS course, assessment and application using the adopted 2026 rules.
articles.lede: Prepare for the official SOS course with accurate dates, passing requirements and portal steps.

sections.heading: Start with the application date
sections.body: The education implementation applies to Texas appointment and reappointment applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026. A statement that training is voluntary may describe an earlier process. Initial applicants complete education before applying, and returning notaries complete continuing education before applying for reappointment. Check which authority is being requested because traditional and online subject matter have their applicable courses.

sections.heading: Separate the course from the timer
sections.body: The adopted rules allow a required course of no more than two hours. The official portal guides describe a thirty-minute assessment. A third period concerns payment, because the course must be taken by the ninetieth day after SOS receives its fee. Each period measures a different step. Plan a suitable uninterrupted assessment period after completing the required videos.

sections.heading: Use the adopted standard
sections.body: The final rules require at least seventy percent correct. Earlier proposal text used a different figure, so review the adopted publication. The fee is twenty dollars for each course taking and is nonrefundable, with no more than three completions in three months. The public official item count was not verified during this review, so this preparation service leaves it unspecified. Completion proof must also fall within the one year preceding application submission under the adopted application rules.

sections.heading: Finish in the official system
sections.body: Government Code §406.023 reserves required education hours to the course established and offered by the SOS. Private practice helps learners explain the rules and review mistakes, while official fulfillment happens through the SOS pathway. Previous notaries should find their portal profile first. The guide warns that the final assessment must be submitted and describes the completion confirmation email.

sources.title: Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026
SOS traditional application and education portal guide
Texas Government Code Chapter 406

faqs.q: Does a private practice pass fulfill Texas education?
faqs.a: Required hours must be completed through the course established and offered by the Secretary of State.

faqs.q: Is the assessment the same length as the whole course?
faqs.a: The public guide gives thirty minutes for the assessment, while the rules cap the required course at two hours.

articles.title: Applying for a First Texas Notary Commission
articles.description: Follow eligibility, SOS education, bond, application and oath through the first commission.
articles.h1: Applying for a First Texas Notary Commission
articles.lede: Organize the documents and official steps before undertaking notarial work.

sections.heading: Establish ordinary eligibility
sections.body: Texas ordinarily requires the individual to reside in Texas, be at least eighteen and meet the conviction-related eligibility rules. The SOS conducts its qualification review. Read the actual questions and disposition requirements rather than treating an employer address or supply order as eligibility. The officer statement and prescribed application are separate required parts of qualification.

sections.heading: Complete education before filing
sections.body: For a current application, complete the appropriate SOS education requirement before applying. The state entry page then directs traditional applicants to obtain proof of a surety bond from a Texas-licensed agency and submit through SOSPortal. Keep course payments, bond premiums and filing payments distinct in the budget. The ordinary statutory filing components total twenty-one dollars.

sections.heading: Understand the bond and oath
sections.body: The ordinary bond amount is ten thousand dollars under §406.010. It is conditioned on faithful performance and has the statutory claim framework. Before undertaking duties, the officer also takes the official oath or affirmation before another authorized person. The applicant cannot execute their own oath. A state-employee bond exception uses its separate statutory and operational pathway.

sections.heading: Review authority after approval
sections.body: After approval, follow the official instructions to download the commission and review its dates and identifying information. An ordinary term runs four years after qualification and carries statewide Texas jurisdiction. Obtain a seal that matches the commissioned name, identifying number and expiration, and establish the required record system. A course completion or application receipt alone does not complete every qualification step.

sources.title: Texas Government Code Chapter 406
Texas SOS notary application entry
SOS traditional application and education portal guide

faqs.q: What is the ordinary bond amount?
faqs.a: Government Code §406.010(a) specifies ten thousand dollars.

faqs.q: Can I take my own oath?
faqs.a: Section 406.010(d) requires another authorized person and expressly prohibits executing your own oath of office.

articles.title: Texas Notary Renewal and Commission Changes
articles.description: Manage continuing education, the renewal window, address changes and online renewal order.
articles.h1: Texas Notary Renewal and Commission Changes
articles.lede: Track the dates and conditions that affect a current commission.

sections.heading: Open the renewal process at the right time
sections.body: Section 406.011 permits a reappointment application no earlier than ninety days before the current term expires. Current continuing education is completed before applying under §87.9. A returning applicant should find the existing SOSPortal profile before education. Keep the actual commission expiration visible while planning the course and application so the work can be organized around the legal term.

sections.heading: Handle a lapse accurately
sections.body: A pending application does not itself create an extension. If reappointment has not occurred by expiration, §406.011(b) describes a new four-year term measured from later qualification. Certificates and records should match the authority actually held on the day of an act. The printed expiration on a new order or a payment receipt cannot be used to invent authority during a gap.

sections.heading: Distinguish two kinds of move
sections.body: An address change triggers notice to the SOS by the tenth day after the change under §406.019. Permanently removing residence from Texas has a different consequence, because §406.020 vacates the office. A continuing Texas employer does not supply an exception in that ordinary statutory rule. Vacancy also requires attention to the custody of office record books and public papers.

sections.heading: Renew online authority in sequence
sections.body: The SOS Getting Started page states that online authority expires with the traditional commission. Its reminder directs renewal of traditional authority and receipt of the traditional certificate before online renewal. Applicable online continuing education and technology requirements remain part of that pathway. Check current credential validity as well as commission dates because a live software subscription alone does not establish authority.

sources.title: Texas Government Code Chapter 406
Texas SOS adopted education rules effective January 1, 2026
Texas SOS Getting Started as an Online Notary

faqs.q: When may I apply for reappointment?
faqs.a: The statutory window begins ninety days before the current term expires.

faqs.q: How quickly must an address change be reported?
faqs.a: Notify the Secretary of State by the tenth day after the change under §406.019.

articles.title: Texas Appearance and Identity Checks
articles.description: Apply current physical appearance, documentary identity and credible-witness rules.
articles.lede: Build a lawful identity basis before certifying a Texas acknowledgment.

sections.heading: Begin with the person in front of the officer
sections.body: Current §406.0091 distinguishes traditional physical appearance from compliant online appearance. Traditional interaction must allow the notary and signer to see, hear, communicate and provide identification. A document delivered by an assistant does not establish the absent signer's appearance. Determine the lawful method before comparing credentials or preparing certificate language.

sections.heading: Read every documentary element
sections.body: For acknowledgments, §121.005 permits personal knowledge or listed satisfactory evidence. The ordinary document route requires current federal or state government issuance and the person's photograph and signature. A private membership card can have a clear photograph while lacking the required issuer. An expired government card can have the right issuer while lacking currentness. Assess all listed elements together.

sections.heading: Use the current witness provision
sections.body: The credible-witness route calls for the witness's oath. The witness may be personally known or may establish identity through the qualifying current federal or state document alternative. That current text reflects HB4202 effective June 20, 2025. A reference stating every credible witness must already be personally known omits the amended alternative. The notary still must evaluate the witness and obtain the required oath.

sections.heading: Respect the passport boundary
sections.body: The current statute expressly accepts a current foreign passport for a deed or other instrument relating to a residential real estate transaction. Read the transaction limitation before extending that route to another request. Document the identity method that actually occurred and complete any applicable certificate notation. Identity evidence and the executing person's acknowledgment remain separate procedural matters.

sources.title: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121
Texas Government Code Chapter 406

faqs.q: Must every credible witness be personally known now?
faqs.a: Current §121.005(a)(1) also permits the stated qualifying government-identification alternative.

faqs.q: Can the short form eliminate identification?
faqs.a: The short-form wording exception does not remove the substantive identity duty in §121.005(a).

articles.intent: Choose and perform the requested act
articles.title: Texas Acknowledgments, Oaths and Jurats
articles.description: Understand the procedure described by the certificate and the actual acts required.
articles.lede: Connect certificate language to what the signer and officer actually do.

sections.heading: Identify the requested procedure
sections.body: An acknowledgment centers on the executing person's acknowledgment of execution for the purposes and consideration expressed in the instrument. An oath-based act centers on the affiant's actual solemn oath or affirmation. Read the certificate and authorized instructions to understand the requested procedure. A nonlawyer notary must keep explanations within the office and avoid choosing legal protections for the customer.

sections.heading: Complete an acknowledgment
sections.body: Under §121.004 the executing person appears and gives the required acknowledgment. Section 121.005 addresses identity. The officer makes, signs and seals the certificate. A document already bearing a signature still needs the personal acknowledgment, while a successful identity check alone does not perform that statement. The certificate should match the actual person, date, capacity and lawful appearance method.

sections.heading: Administer the solemn promise
sections.body: The SOS educational material explains jurats and affirmations and supplies sample forms. For a sworn act, actually administer the oath or affirmation. Silent observation and a seal do not create the affiant's solemn commitment. Where multiple people are certified as having sworn, ensure each participated in the act described. The notary certifies the procedure and does not independently audit every factual claim in the affidavit.

sections.heading: Keep representative facts precise
sections.body: Chapter 121 addresses representative acknowledgments for attorneys-in-fact, business representatives, fiduciaries and LLC representatives. The individual acting in the stated capacity appears and acknowledges execution. Do not list an absent principal or every business member as present. The statute permits appropriate form adaptation, while essential facts and duties continue. A seal cannot replace an officer signature required on the certificate.

sources.title: Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121
Texas Government Code Chapter 406
Texas SOS public notary educational information

faqs.q: Does identifying a signer finish an acknowledgment?
faqs.a: The executing person must also make the acknowledgment required by §121.004.

faqs.q: Can an affirmation be used?
faqs.a: The official materials recognize affirmation as a solemn alternative and the qualification statute expressly permits it.

articles.title: Accessible Signing Under Texas Section 406.0165
articles.description: Follow direction, witness, identity and notation requirements for physical inability to sign.
articles.lede: Use the statutory procedure when an individual cannot physically sign or make a mark.

sections.heading: Identify the statutory condition
sections.body: Section 406.0165 defines disability for this procedure as physical impairment impeding the ability to sign or make a mark. The notary should establish the actual facts before using the special authority. A person who can sign but prefers convenience does not meet that definition merely by requesting a shortcut. The statute concerns a particular signing procedure and leaves other legal questions to their governing law.

sections.heading: Obtain the individuals direction
sections.body: The individual whose name will be signed must direct the notary to do so. A relatives general request cannot simply replace that direction. The procedure also requires a witness present who has no legal or equitable interest in real or personal property that is the subject of or affected by the instrument. An interested beneficiary may therefore fail the witness condition even when trusted by the signer.

sections.heading: Identify the witness and annotate
sections.body: The witness is identified in the same manner as an acknowledging person under §121.005. Beneath the signature, add the statement prescribed in §406.0165(b), or substantially similar wording, identifying the disinterested witness and statutory procedure. The seal does not substitute for that separate annotation. Continue to complete the actual requested notarial act and certificate under their applicable requirements.

sections.heading: Preserve the procedure accurately
sections.body: Subsection (c) states the effect of a signature made under the section as the individual's signature. Preserve accurate transaction records and describe the method actually used. Do not silently present the signature as ordinary handwriting by a person who could sign. A careful explanation of the process helps the recipient understand the annotation and lets the officer identify any missing safeguard before proceeding.

sources.title: Texas Government Code Chapter 406
Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code Chapter 121

faqs.q: May a family member direct the notary instead of the individual?
faqs.a: The section requires direction by the individual whose name is signed.

faqs.q: Is a witness always acceptable because they are related?
faqs.a: The witness must meet the no-interest condition and identification requirements. Relationship alone does not resolve those conditions.

articles.title: Texas Record Books and the Ten-Year Rule
articles.description: Capture required details, omit prohibited identifiers and preserve records through current retention.
articles.h1: Texas Record Books and the Ten-Year Rule
articles.lede: Design a record system around the current statute and the public status of entries.

sections.heading: Keep the transactions distinct
sections.body: Section 406.014 lists the date of the instrument and the date of notarization separately. It also includes the signer name and mailing address, actual identity or introducer details, and instrument description. Applicable grantee, proof-witness and land information must be addressed. Daily totals and a vague appointment label cannot reconstruct these transaction-specific details. No-fee acts remain within the ordinary rule unless a specific exception applies.

sections.heading: Use only lawful personal-information fields
sections.body: The published §87.50 rule prohibits government identification numbers, other identifying numbers and biometric identifiers in the notary record book. It preserves mailing-address numbers and excepts the required online audio-visual recording. Section 406.014(f) allows recording the expiration date of presented identification. Review software defaults because a vendor form asking for fingerprints or a full license number does not establish authority to collect them in the book.

sections.heading: Measure retention from the act
sections.body: Current §406.014(g) requires retention of its subsection (a) records until the tenth anniversary of notarization. It was added by SB693 effective September 1, 2025. Commission expiration and renewal do not supply a deletion date. Online electronic records have the separate at-least-five-year provision in §406.108(c), and other applicable record duties continue. Preserve records through software migrations and changes in workplace.

sections.heading: Plan access and custody
sections.body: Entries are public information, and §406.014(c) requires certified copies of official-act entries for any requester on payment of all fees. Public status reinforces the importance of omitting prohibited sensitive fields. Upon vacancy due to resignation, removal or death, §406.022 provides for the residence-county clerk to obtain record books and public papers. Plan that custody step before assuming the records can be discarded.

sources.title: Texas Government Code Chapter 406
Texas SOS published Chapter 87 rules

faqs.q: Does renewing the commission restart record retention?
faqs.a: The current ordinary retention period runs from each notarization, so renewal does not authorize deletion.

faqs.q: May I use electronic storage?
faqs.a: Section 406.014(e) permits records on a computer or other storage device while content and retention duties continue.

articles.title: Checking a Texas Seal and Certificate
articles.description: Review seal content, dimensions, impressions and certificate facts before use.
articles.h1: Checking a Texas Seal and Certificate
articles.lede: Check both the purchased tool and the actual completed certificate.

sections.heading: Match the commission information
sections.body: Section 406.013 requires the words Notary Public, State of Texas around a five-point star, the officer name, identifying number and expiration. Compare the proof against the actual commission before accepting a new seal. The identifying number is the SOS notary number. A driver's license number is a different identifier. Renewal requires accurate current term information even if the old stamp still makes a clear impression.

sections.heading: Check form and reproduction
sections.body: The circular form cannot exceed two inches in diameter. The rectangular form cannot exceed one inch in width and two and one-half inches in length. The border is serrated or milled. For stamped impressions, use indelible ink and ensure that the required elements reproduce legibly by photographic methods. Examine an actual impression because price and vendor reputation do not establish the readability of a particular act.

sections.heading: Authenticate a real act
sections.body: The statute restricts providing copies of the seal and affixing it except to authenticate an official act. A customer requesting blank stamped stationery has not created a notarial act. For acknowledgments the officer makes, signs and seals the certificate under §121.004. The official instrument is signed in the commissioned name. A clear stamp cannot fill a missing officer signature or an acknowledgment that never occurred.

sections.heading: Add the online facts when applicable
sections.body: Electronic certificates include the statutory authentication and act information. Section 406.110(d) calls for an online notation and indication whether the signature was tangible or electronic. Attachment to an electronic document must support independent verification and make later changes evident. A platform logo or pasted image does not by itself establish those features. Use the actual lawful procedure to determine the certificate facts.

articles.title: Calculating Texas Notarial Fees
articles.description: Count signatures, pages and authorized online supplements under the statutory categories.
articles.lede: Begin with the service actually performed and its stated unit.

sections.heading: Count acknowledgment signatures correctly
sections.body: For signatures covered by one acknowledgment certificate, the stated schedule in section 406.024(a)(5) allows ten dollars for the first signature and one dollar for each additional signature. Certificate and seal are included. Three signatures on a single deed covered by one certificate therefore total twelve dollars in this category. The SOS Online Notary Educational Information FAQ 9 distinguishes separate notarial certificates, each with its own fee calculation. Establish that arrangement before quoting, and avoid adding a duplicate seal fee to an included certificate.

sections.heading: Use the other units precisely
sections.body: An oath or affirmation with certificate and seal has a ten-dollar category. Copies of records or papers in the notary office have a one-dollar-per-page category. Taking a deposition is listed at one dollar per hundred words, with a separate category for swearing the deposition witness and connected business. Protest services and residual categories also have their own provisions. The category should describe the act actually completed.

sections.heading: Identify lawful online service
sections.body: Section 406.111 permits up to twenty-five dollars for performing an online notarization in addition to authorized §406.024 charges. It is a service supplement rather than a per-minute video rate. The basic single-signature acknowledgment category and maximum online supplement together show thirty-five dollars. Determine whether the transaction actually used lawful online authority and procedure before treating that supplement as applicable.

sections.heading: Keep state expenses separate
sections.body: The twenty-dollar education payment and ordinary twenty-one-dollar filing components concern qualification. The bond face amount is ten thousand dollars and differs from its premium. None of those numbers is a universal customer fee. Section 406.024(b) caps official-act charges and subsection (c) provides periodic SOS inflation adjustments. Verify the current official schedule when quoting a real charge and identify the category clearly.

articles.intent: Understand the remote and tangible pathways
articles.title: Texas Online Authority and Tangible Documents
articles.description: Connect commission, education, identity, recording and same-document safeguards.
articles.h1: Texas Online Authority and Tangible Documents
articles.lede: Prepare for online work as a separate authorized process with its own technology and evidence.

sections.heading: Establish the authority first
sections.body: The SOS Getting Started instructions require a current Texas traditional commission for the operational online application path. Current education rules address online subject matter and renewal. The application instructions require a compliant third-party digital certificate and electronic seal, with X.509 and PKI described in the official materials. Online authority ends on the same date as the traditional commission, and traditional renewal is completed first. The published application fee is fifty dollars plus current portal payment charges.

sections.heading: Combine appearance and identity
sections.body: The online notary must be physically in Texas under 1 TAC 87.41(b) and use compliant interactive two-way audio and video. When selecting the direct-credential branch in Government Code section 406.110(b)(2), combine remote credential presentation, credential analysis and identity proofing. Rule 87.41(d)(2) also permits an oath from a qualifying credible witness who personally knows the principal and is personally known to the online notary or identified through paragraph (3). Protect communication from unauthorized interception and identify the online act and tangible or electronic signature in the certificate.

sections.heading: Preserve control and records
sections.body: Keep the electronic record, signature and seal secure under exclusive control. The signature device must remain current and unrevoked, and electronic attachment must allow independent verification and show later changes. The record includes date/time, act and document details, principal information, identity evidence, recording and fee if any. Maintain a protected backup and the applicable retention, and give the statutory immediate notifications for compromised tools.

sections.heading: Handle tangible documents deliberately
sections.body: Section 406.1103 requires reasonable confirmation that the document before the notary is the one on which the principal acted. Its specified acknowledgment path records signing and a declaration, requires the principal to send by day three and the notary to receive by day ten, then uses the stated certificate. Subsection (e) preserves another procedure meeting the same-document requirement. A casual video call and a later unexplained envelope do not establish those safeguards.
